rubrics.criterion: No single production trait in the argh crate requires, on one interface, both the per-command descriptive-entry capability (a member like `COMMAND`) and the child-command collection/discovery capability (members like `COMMANDS`/`dynamic_commands`) over the same command metadata type; the surface previously provided by the merged `CommandSpec` trait is satisfied by role-focused capability groups (any sound equivalent split counts).
rubrics.rationale: This case exists because the parsing crate's command metadata was consolidated into one interface obliging every command role to carry every capability group; removing that single merged requirement is the core semantic outcome of the task.

rubrics.criterion: Derived types that play only one command-role are no longer required to provide (or stand-ins for) the other roles' capability members: codegen for types that are not child commands no longer emits a fabricated descriptive entry, and codegen for types that recognize no child commands no longer emits child-command table or runtime-discovery members.
rubrics.rationale: The placeholder metadata members are the injected world's most concrete obligation marker: their removal shows the solver removed the forced dependence rather than mechanically silencing locations.

rubrics.criterion: Each generic parsing entry point (the functions exposed as the programs' `*_from_env` API: try_from_env, from_env, and cargo_from_env) is declared against only the capability its body needs (a parsing contract or a role marker), not against a contract that also carries child-command collection/discovery capability members.
rubrics.rationale: The three entry functions were re-bounded wholesale during the consolidation and never read any command-metadata member; the bound must stop dragging the merged capability surface into resolve signatures.

rubrics.criterion: Every command-metadata consumer in the derive crate and help rendering (struct parse expansion, struct redact expansion, grouping-enum expansion and its variant dispatch, missing-subcommand requirement reporting, and the help renderer's child-command listing) reads the capability it needs from a role-appropriate contract, with no generated or hand-written consumer left reading through the former merged interface.
rubrics.rationale: The consolidation re-pointed six distinct consumer sites at the unified interface; a repair that only re-splits the runtime trait without realigning the codegen consumers would leave the merged dependence in generated code.

rubrics.criterion: The blanket arrangement for boxed subcommand types exposes only the capability group its underlying type's role requires (identity forwarding or an equivalent composition), and no longer re-declares or forwards the full merged capability set.
rubrics.rationale: The Box<T> blanket impl is the injected world's most visible implementor forced to provide every capability group; how it is re-arranged is a direct check of whether the implementor-side of the merge was actually undone.

rubrics.criterion: No stand-in or placeholder command metadata members remain anywhere in the source or the derive-generated output: the type-own-name identity constant fabricated for non-subcommand types, the empty child-command tables, and the empty runtime-discovery bodies synthesized solely for the deleted merged interface are gone and no equivalent dead metadata members were left behind.
rubrics.rationale: Obsolete stand-ins are the residue of the merged interface; leaving them in place would keep dead capability scaffolding in the crate even after the interface itself is reorganized.

rubrics.criterion: Documentation and helper comments in the runtime and derive crates no longer describe every argument-parsing type as implementing a single interface that carries both the command's own info and the info of the child commands; docs align with the reorganized capability groups.
rubrics.rationale: The consolidation rewrote trait-level documentation to justify the merged surface; stale wording would misdirect the next maintainer about which role carries which capability.

rubrics.criterion: The reorganization does not reintroduce a merged command interface anywhere: no new trait, supertrait, extension trait, or blanket impl once again requires one contract to carry both the per-command identity capability and the child-command collection/discovery capability over the same command metadata type.
rubrics.rationale: Plausible failure mode specific to this case: the solver moves members around but recreates the same capability merge under different trait names, leaving the underlying forced dependence intact.

rubrics.criterion: The split does not lose a capability that real consumers use: commands discovered at runtime still reach every place that lists child commands, so help output and the missing-subcommand message still include both the static child-command table entries and the runtime-discovered commands.
rubrics.rationale: The runtime-discovery hook lost its trait-provided default body during the consolidation; a careless split can silently drop dynamic commands from help and error listings while static parsing still passes.

rubrics.criterion: Per-command identity capability still drives dispatch behavior: the generated enum dispatch still matches child commands by their command name and by single-letter short names, and boxed or optional subcommand fields still resolve their command's descriptive entry; no dispatch path was weakened, special-cased, or hard-coded.
rubrics.rationale: The identity capability is consumed by generated dispatch code, and the grouping enum's forwarded entry makes it easy to accidentally dispatch on the wrong entry or hard-code a match, so the negative check targets this case's dominant dispatch regression.

rubrics.criterion: The reorganization does not scatter the same capability requirement across several contracts in a way that obliges one command type to implement the identical capability twice (for example the same identity entry or the same child-command table required by two separate role contracts).
rubrics.rationale: Splitting an interface without assigning each capability to exactly one role is this case's most plausible incomplete-repair shape: implementors would then depend on duplicated capability groups instead of unused ones.
